metadata.remarks:
Server Attestation and Trust defines the capability to establish cryptographic and measurable confidence in the integrity of servers and workloads. This includes verification of boot state, firmware, host configuration, and, where applicable, workload identity. Attestation provides a trust signal stronger than configuration or monitoring alone and enables high-assurance execution decisions.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance related to server integrity verification. Controls are intentionally scoped to trust establishment and do not include configuration enforcement, patching, or runtime threat detection.

components.title: Hardware Root of Trust
components.description: Use of hardware-based mechanisms to anchor trust in server platforms.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Use cryptographic mechanisms to establish trusted execution foundations.

components.title: Boot Attestation
components.description: Verification of server boot integrity, including firmware, bootloader, and kernel stages.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Verify software and firmware integrity during system startup.

components.title: Host and Platform Integrity
components.description: Measurement and verification of the server host platform state beyond initial boot.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Continuously or periodically verify host platform integrity measurements.

components.title: Workload Attestation
components.description: Verification that workloads are executing on trusted hosts and in approved execution contexts.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Use attestation results to authorize workload execution or access.
